   118|func downloadModel(from remoteURL: URL) async throws -> URL {

   120|    let local = cache.appendingPathComponent(remoteURL.lastPathComponent)
   121|    if FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: local.path),
   122|       let attrs = try? FileManager.default.attributesOfItem(atPath: local.path),
   123|       let size = attrs[.size] as? Int, size > 0 {
   124|        return local
   125|    }
   126|    let (temp, response) = try await URLSession.shared.download(from: remoteURL)
   127|    guard let http = response as? HTTPURLResponse, (200...299).contains(http.statusCode) else {
   128|        throw URLError(.badServerResponse)
   129|    }
   130|    try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: local)
   131|    try FileManager.default.moveItem(at: temp, to: local)
   132|    return local
   133|}

**Regarding images — yes, I can find them for you.** I'd source high-quality photos from Unsplash for each mountain. Most of the iconic peaks (Everest, K2, Denali, Matterhorn, Mont Blanc, Kilimanjaro, etc.) have excellent free photography available. For the Colorado 14ers and lesser-known peaks, some might be harder to find, but I can cover the majority.

Want me to go ahead and implement this? I'd:
1. Add an `imageUrl` field to each mountain in your data
2. Source Unsplash images for all the mountains
3. Rebuild the detail screen with the photo hero layout shown in the mockup
